summary: @servicetitan/standalone-core-feature-gates preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React feature-gate library but its declared preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`) is an obfuscated dropper. setup.mjs itself uses obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers and string-indirection maps to hide its behavior: it downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (pinned to bun-v1.3.13), extracts it to a temp directory, marks the binary executable, and then invokes `execFileSync(<bun>, ['math_init.js'], {stdio:'inherit'})`. The sibling `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle (rotated string array with a `arr.push(arr.shift())` shift routine, hex-named globals, all literals indexed through the array) whose contents cannot be audited. Using an alternate JS runtime (Bun) to execute the payload bypasses Node-based install-time scanners; the filename `math_init` is a cover story unrelated to a feature-gate library. Running `npm install` on this package executes attacker-controlled, opaque code on the installer's host at install time, and the scope name (`@servicetitan/*`) impersonates the well-known ServiceTitan organization.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
